# 04 Concept to Interview Map

This document provides a structured mapping between fundamental Discrete Mathematics concepts and Algorithm Analysis techniques to common technical interview problem categories and LeetCode patterns. It serves as a guide for identifying which theoretical tools are relevant for different types of practical challenges.

## 1. Discrete Math Concepts & Interview Relevance

| Discrete Math Concept      | Interview Problem Category / LeetCode Pattern  | How it Applies                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Relevant Worked Problems |
| :------------------------- | :--------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :----------------------- |
| **Logic & Quantifiers**    | Correctness Proofs, Edge Cases, Pre/Post Conditions, Invariants, Graph Properties | Reasoning about algorithm correctness (e.g., loop invariants, pre/post conditions). Formulating precise problem definitions. Handling edge cases.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Valid Parentheses, Insertion Sort (Correctness Proof) |
| **Set Theory & Relations** | Graphs (Nodes & Edges), Equivalence Classes, Data Grouping, Subsets                 | Modeling relationships between data elements (e.g., connected components in graphs, friendships in social networks). Grouping data into equivalence classes. Generating subsets.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                       | Number of Islands, Subsets, Majority Element |
| **Functions**              | Mappings (Hash Tables), Transformations, One-to-One / Onto Properties, Bijections   | Designing hash functions (collisions, distribution). Understanding data transformations. Establishing unique mappings or reversible operations (encryption/decryption).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Two Sum, Hash Table based problems |
| **Number Theory**          | Modular Arithmetic, Hashing, Bit Manipulation, GCD/LCM, Prime Factorization         | Designing hash functions. Handling overflow/underflow. Cryptography (e.g., RSA). Optimizing number-based algorithms. `(n mod d)` calculations.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   | Two Sum, Majority Element, Cryptography examples |
| **Counting & Combinatorics** | Permutations, Combinations, Subsets, Probability, Dynamic Programming (Counting)    | Calculating number of possible arrangements or selections. Analyzing complexity of algorithms that explore combinations. Understanding probability in randomized algorithms or search spaces.                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Subsets, Tossing Coins, Dice Rolls |
| **Mathematical Induction** | Correctness Proofs (Recursive Algorithms, Loop Invariants), Properties of Sequences | Proving correctness for recursive algorithms (e.g., Merge Sort, Fibonacci). Establishing properties of data structures or mathematical formulas. Proving loop invariants.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | Merge Sort (Correctness Proof), Valid Parentheses (Inductive Proof) |
| **Recurrence Relations**   | Dynamic Programming, Divide & Conquer, Recursive Algorithm Analysis                 | Modeling the runtime of recursive algorithms. Solving problems by breaking them into smaller, self-similar subproblems. Deriving explicit formulas for sequences.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Merge Sort (Time Complexity), Climbing Stairs |
| **Expected Value**         | Randomized Algorithms, Probabilistic Analysis, Average-Case Performance             | Analyzing the average performance of algorithms that use randomness. Risk assessment in business decisions.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                | Kth Largest Element (Randomized Quickselect), A/B Testing intuition |

## 2. Algorithm Analysis Techniques & Interview Relevance

| Algorithm Analysis Technique | Interview Problem Category / LeetCode Pattern | How it Applies                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            | Relevant Worked Problems |
| :--------------------------- | :-------------------------------------------- | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | :----------------------- |
| **Asymptotic Notation**      | Time/Space Complexity Analysis, Comparing Algorithms                                  | Characterizing the efficiency of algorithms (Big O, Big Omega, Big Theta). Essential for discussing scalability and choosing the right algorithm for different input sizes.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        | All algorithms (e.g., Insertion Sort vs. Merge Sort) |
| **Loop Invariants**          | Correctness Proofs, Iterative Algorithms                                          | Proving correctness of iterative algorithms. Ensuring a property holds true at each step of a loop.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Insertion Sort (Correctness Proof), Linear Search (Correctness Proof) |
| **Divide & Conquer**         | Sorting (Merge Sort), Binary Search, Tree Traversals, Matrix Multiplication         | Breaking a problem into smaller subproblems of the same type, solving them independently, and combining their results. Efficiently solves problems like sorting, searching, and structural traversals.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         | Merge Sort, Invert Binary Tree, Binary Search Tree problems |
| **Recursion**                | Tree/Graph Traversal, Dynamic Programming, Backtracking, Functional Algorithms        | Solving problems by defining a solution in terms of simpler instances of the same problem. Crucial for understanding tree structures, search algorithms (DFS/BFS intuition), and dynamic programming base cases.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             | Invert Binary Tree, Climbing Stairs, Number of Islands |
| **Master Theorem**           | Recurrence Relation Solving (Divide & Conquer)                                    | Quickly determining the asymptotic complexity of recurrence relations that arise from divide-and-conquer algorithms.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Merge Sort, Quick Sort |
| **Space Complexity**         | Memory Optimization, Data Structure Choice, Trade-offs                                | Analyzing how much memory an algorithm uses. Essential for designing memory-efficient solutions, especially in embedded systems or large-scale data processing. Often a trade-off with time complexity.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                      | Merge Sort (O(n) auxiliary space), In-place sorts (O(1) space) |
| **Time-Space Trade-offs**    | Caching, Hash Tables, Dynamic Programming (Memoization)                           | Understanding when to use more memory to achieve faster computation, or vice-versa. Key design decision in many algorithms (e.g., hash tables use more space for faster lookups; dynamic programming uses memory for memoization to avoid recomputation).                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Two Sum (Hash Table), Dynamic Programming problems (e.g., Fibonacci with memoization) |
